Make the changes by hand: in Game.kt, pass *KubrikoWiring.createManagers(firstScene = "main").toTypedArray() to Kubriko.newInstance instead of a SceneLoader, in GameEntryPoint.kt, add override fun createCustomManagers() = KubrikoWiring.createManagers(isInSceneEditor = true), and in the desktop Main.kt, set KubrikoWiring.isLoggingEnabled = System.getProperty("kubriko.creator.logging").toBoolean() and KubrikoWiring.firstSceneOverride = System.getProperty("kubriko.creator.scene") before the application starts, and in the web Main.kt, call useValidBrowserLanguage() first, as a new project's does, so a browser started under the POSIX locale still draws texts. Think of your game as a film. Pick something on the left to work on, or make something new with its + button.
Actor types are the characters of your game. Each one plays its role: Events say when it acts, and Blocks say what it does.
Managers work behind the scenes for the whole game: they keep the score, show texts on the screen, and react to keys.
Scenes are where the story happens. Open one and drag your Actor types in to set the stage.
Press Play whenever you want to see your game in action.
